newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks soar to record on rates hope.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks soar to record on rates hope.

text.p: Mexican stocks soared to notch up their third record close in as many sessions Tuesday.
Traders said forecast falls in primary interest rates, expected favourable 1996 earnings reports and steady gains on Wall Street coaxed buyers into the market.
The leading IPC share index ended up 48.92 points, or 1.26 percent, at a record of 3,938.69.
Trading volume was brisk at 103.8 million shares.
"The market well withstood intraday profit-taking, foreigners are still stepping in and we expect (primary) rates to fall," a desk trader said.

A Reuters survey of eight money market traders in Mexico City showed they expected Banco de Mexico to assign bellwether 28-day Cetes, or Treasury bills, at 18.86 percent at its weekly auction of government securities.
This would be a fall of 0.60 percentage point since last week's auction and a rate unseen since an abrupt devaluation of the peso sent Mexican financial markets into a tailspin in December 1994.
Banco de Mexico was due to announce auction results at after the close of trade.
Analysts drew attention to 1996 earnings posted by beverage firm Femsa Coca-Cola and steelmaker Ahmsa, saying both contained welcome surprises that boded well for companies that had yet to report.
Ahmsa nominal shares gained 1.30 pesos (17 cents) to 17.78 pesos ($2.29), while Femsa Coca-Cola L shares ended up 1.80 pesos (23 cents) at 27.00 pesos ($3.48).
Both Femsa Coca-Cola and Ahmsa ended among the leading percentage gainers.
Cement firm GCC ended up 18 centavos (2 cents) at 9.08 pesos ($1.17), while retail chain Autrey gained 16 centavos (2 cents) to 17.50 pesos ($2.25).
Analysts also said that gains on Wall Street propped up the bourse.
"The Dow Jones (Industrial average) helped us, albeit relatively, as lack of volatility on Wall Street is a benfit," said Rodolfo Campuzano, an analyst at the Invex brokerage.
The Dow ended up 0.38 percent, or 29.63 points, at 7,037.83 points.
On the broad market, 122 stocks changed hands, with gainers heavily outnumbering decliners, by 70 to 28.
Traders said soft drinks bottlers Ggemex CPO shares were notable gainers, up 94 centavos (12 cents) to 13.70 pesos ($1.76) on favourable earnings by Femsa Coca-Cola.
Femsa Coca-Cola's holding company Femsa B shares also gained strongly, ending up 1.90 pesos (24 cents) at 32.95 pesos ($4.24).

Financially-troubled autoparts maket Iasasa headed the decliners' list, off three centavos (1 cent) to 50 centavos (six cents), followed by retail stock Commerci, which fell 38 centavos (5 cents) to 6.52 pesos (84 cents).
